subject: Qualification recap — prompt set & harness agreement
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@edgecommerce.com>, Tom Barnes <tbarnes@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Qualification recap — prompt set & harness agreement

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment. Below is a concise recap and the things we agreed to validate for the performance qualification run. Please confirm or flag anything missing.

High-level goals (your ask):
- Streaming chat SLO: 95% of tokens streamed within 250ms, end-to-end response completion under 450ms for 64-token replies at peak concurrency.
- Sustained throughput target: 150 reqs/sec with a concurrency ceiling of 40 concurrent connections during steady-state.
- Reproducibility: deterministic eval for the prompt set and measurement definitions so both teams can reproduce numbers.

Benchmark methodology (proposed / what we will hand over):
1) Prompt set: see attached edge-benchmark-promptset-v1.json (categorised: transactional, contextual recall, retrieval-augmented).
2) Harness: reference harness in GitHub (link below) — we will provide a container image and a run script.
3) Measurement definitions (attached measurement-defs.md): warm vs cold cache, tokenization normalization, what counts as an "inference token", how streaming latency is measured (per-chunk latency vs first-token vs completion).
4) Environment spec: model sha/weights, quantization profile, CPU/GPU machine types, kernel selection notes.
5) Repro steps: seed values, RNG control, fixed batch/sequence-length distributions, and a recorded traffic trace we can replay for parity.

Open questions we covered on the call:
- Do you want tail metrics at p95 or p99 for SLA gating? (you asked for p95 for streaming token latency, p99 for completion)
- Is synthetic traffic acceptable for the initial run, or do you prefer a replay of production traces?
- Whether the run should be on Redwood Hosted (quick) or Redwood Dedicated (closest to your production environment).

Next steps / owners / dates:
- Redwood to share: prompt set, measurement-defs.md, and a reproducible harness container (Hannah) — by 2026-11-03 EOD.
- EdgeCommerce to confirm: target SLO definitions (p95 vs p99), preferred run window, and whether production traces will be shared (Alicia/Tom) — by 2026-11-04 EOD.
- Redwood infra (Sean) to propose two feasible run slots and cost estimates for Dedicated vs Hosted test runs — by 2026-11-05.

Attachments: edge-benchmark-promptset-v1.json, measurement-defs.md (see attached). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/EDGE-4392

Thanks — aim is to have a reproducible baseline so we can iterate on quantization and routing without breaking parity.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@edgecommerce.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Qualification recap — prompt set & harness agreement

Thanks Hannah — that matches my notes. A couple quick clarifications: 
1) For the SLO gating we'll use p95 for per-token streaming latency and p99 for end-to-end completion latency.
2) For the initial run we'd be fine with synthetic traffic if you ship a replayable trace we can compare to later.

We'd like the run to mirror our production model (same quant and same model checkpoint) — I'll confirm the exact checkpoint name and share the trace if you can accept an S3 link.

Can you also include the seed value you plan to use and confirm chunk sizes for streaming flush behavior? Those two will affect determinism.

Alicia
Head of Platform
EdgeCommerce
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia@edgecommerce.com>, Tom Barnes <tbarnes@edgecommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Qualification recap — prompt set & harness agreement (internal next steps)

Forwarding Alicia's confirm. Sean / Monica — see below and the attached protocol PDF (redwood-benchmark-protocol-v1.pdf) which includes a step-by-step runbook. Key internal actions: 
- Sean: please schedule two candidate windows (preferred: 2026-11-10 08:00-12:00 PT and 2026-11-12 20:00-00:00 PT) and estimate cost for a 4-hour Dedicated run vs Hosted burst. Include GPU type and expected token/s.
- Monica: prepare the harness container and bake in the exact seed (20261102-edge-seed-42) and scripts to fix RNG across TF/PyTorch backends. Also include a flag to run with warm cache vs cold cache.
- Hannah: share the prompt set and measurement-defs.md to Alicia (done) and add the HubSpot note on the next call.

Short note on measurement specifics (from protocol):
- Streaming measurement: we will report first-byte latency, per-chunk median, and p95 token latency. Streaming chunk size = 32 tokens by default; we will test 16/32/64 as sensitivity.
- Completion measurement: measured from request send to EOS token, normalized to 64-token output length. Report p50/p95/p99 and median throughput observed.
- Warm vs cold cache: cold = model process start with empty KV cache; warm = after 100 warmup requests.

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-protocol-v1.pdf

Thanks — Sean, Monica, reply with scheduling and notes on any infra constraints.

— Hannah
From: Tom Barnes <tbarnes@edgecommerce.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@edgecommerce.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Qualification recap — prompt set & harness agreement

This looks great. Two final clarifications before we confirm the window: 
- Chunk flush semantics: can you confirm the harness will expose a streaming param to set flush-on-token vs flush-on-chunk? We typically use flush-on-chunk for our client so we need parity.
- Seed and determinism: Alicia and I will share the exact checkpoint name by EOD — if we supply the checkpoint and an S3 trace, will Redwood load the provided weights in the Dedicated run?

If both answers are yes, we can confirm the 2026-11-12 evening window.

Tom
VP Product
EdgeCommerce

On Wed, Nov 3, 2026 at 10:05 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding Alicia's confirm. Sean / Monica — see below and the attached protocol PDF (redwood-benchmark-protocol-v1.pdf) which includes a step-by-step runbook.
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Tom Barnes <tbarnes@edgecommerce.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@edgecommerce.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Qualification recap — prompt set & harness agreement

Tom — yes on both counts:
- The harness exposes --stream-flush-mode with values [on-token, on-chunk]; default is on-chunk. We will include a test matrix for 16/32/64 chunk sizes.
- For Dedicated runs we can load a customer-provided checkpoint from your S3 bucket (you will need to provide a temporary read role). We will run the exact checkpoint you provide and record the model SHA in the run artifact.

Alicia/Tom — once you share the checkpoint name and S3 link we will ingest it into the run image. Monica: please prepare the ingest hook and a short validation step (checksum + model sha) so we have binary parity.

Confirming the 2026-11-12 20:00-00:00 PT slot as tentative pending Sean's infra cost and final S3 details.

— Hannah
